title: Behavioral, senior product manager, weak answers

questions.text: Tell me about a product you owned and what it achieved.
Tell me about a conflict with a stakeholder.
Tell me about a launch that missed its goals.
Tell me about leading people who did not report to you.
Tell me about explaining a hard trade-off to executives.
Tell me about a metric you moved.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Hi Oren, thanks for joining. I'm Sunita, a director of product. This is a thirty minute behavioral conversation.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Hi Sunita, thank you.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How is your day going so far?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Good. Busy, but good.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: I'll ask about three experiences and leave time at the end for your questions.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tell me about a product you owned and what it achieved.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I managed a scheduling product. It had many users and the team was great. We shipped several features and customers liked them.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What did you personally decide, and what changed for customers?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I decided to build calendar sync first. Customers asked for it most, so I put it ahead of reports. Support tickets about missing bookings dropped by about a third.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tell me about a launch that missed its goals.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: We launched a feature and adoption was low. It was a tough market. We learned we should have done more research.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What was your part in that, and what did you change afterward?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I wrote the launch plan. I skipped customer calls because we were late. After that I added a research step to planning, and the next launch hit its target of 1000 users.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tell me about explaining a hard trade-off to executives.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I once told executives we needed more time. They understood. I just explained the situation clearly and they agreed.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Thanks. What questions do you have?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: What is the team size for this role?

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: The product group has six product managers and about forty engineers.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: That's our time. Thanks Oren, the recruiter will follow up within a week.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Thank you, Sunita.

notes: Weak for senior: first answers generic and short; the last one is not probed.
